 A snow gun is covered in snow at Arapahoe Basin Ski Area on Wednesday, Oct. 14, 2026. Two snow-producing systems are moving across Colorado this week. 
 Riley Kisser/Arapahoe Basin Ski Area 
 A stormy pattern that started Sunday, which brought mostly rain, will be followed by another system that is expected to bring snowfall to much of Colorado. 
 As a cold front dropped temperatures across mountain towns in the state, rainfall Sunday transitioned into snowfall Monday, with increasing chances for accumulation as the afternoon turns to night. Summit County is under a winter weather advisory until midnight Monday, with the National Weather Service saying most snow accumulations are expected before 8 p.m. before waning. 
 Between 3-7 inches of snowfall could accumulate, especially at higher elevations such as the Eisenhower-Johnson Memorial Tunnels on Interstate 70 and the mountains of Summit County and the Mosquito Range, according to the advisory. 
 After a brief dry period Tuesday, another storm is expected to hit Colorado Wednesday. While snow totals remain uncertain, OpenSnow stated in a Monday blog post that this fast-moving system could bring another 2-5 inches of snowfall to most ski areas by Thursday morning.
